## Before you stand up

- Run the setup chunk at the top of the Chapter 5 page. It loads the packages and the data.
- Take a few sticky notes of each color as they come around.

**During the hands-on part**

- A pink note on your laptop lid means you are stuck. One of us comes to you.
- A green note means the chunk ran and you are ready to move on.

# After the break

## How we run the two chapters

- We run Chapter 5 together, one chunk at a time. I say the heading before every chunk.
- We stop for questions at the end of every stage.
- Stage 2 is split. You run four of the seven score chunks. I run the three slow ones on the projector.
- Do not use "Run all chunks above" on the Chapter 5 page.
- Chapter 6 is a tour. I run the main chunks on the projector and you watch. The page runs at home in about fifteen seconds, with nothing to skip.

## If a chunk fails, do not stop

Every stage from Stage 2 on opens with one line.

```r
load("checkpoints/stage_1.RData")
```

It restores every object from the end of the previous stage.

Run it. Put up a pink note. Continue with the room.

# Close

## Six stages, two designs

| Stage | Chapter 5, students within schools | Chapter 6, whole schools |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. Estimand | Effect on the treated students | Effect on the treated schools |
| 2. Distance | Fixed effects score, one of eight | School-level score |
| 3. Matching | Global versus within site, one argument | Cluster-global, sequential, network flow |
| 4. Assessment | Pooled and per-school balance | Cluster-level and student-level balance |
| 5. Outcomes | Individual-average and site-average | Individual-, cluster-average, precision-weighted |
| 6. Sensitivity | `sensemakr`, robustness value 57% | `sensemakr`, robustness value 17% |

## What we did not get to

- Chapter 7, the multisite cluster design, which combines the two. It is on the site as a reference.
- The "Try it" block at the end of the Chapter 5 page. It has three variations on the matching call.
- The decision flowcharts, for choosing the options for your own study.
- The "Your own data" template. It lists the five objects to replace.

The site and the repository stay up.

## Questions

Especially questions of this kind:

- Which of the two designs is my study?
- Which stage would I do differently for my data, and why?
